Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reaffirmed that the administration maintains its commitment to the dollar as the global reserve currency. Although the greenback is up 0.33% across its G10 basket over the past week, broader momentum remains constrained by suspected unilateral and coordinated FX interventions that continue to weigh on major bilateral crosses.

Market participants are positioning cautiously ahead of forthcoming UK monthly GDP figures, which threaten to expose lingering growth headwinds. Cross-currents from surging Brent crude and the broader European terms-of-trade deterioration continue to dictate sterling sentiment into today's North American inflation data.

The single currency sits slightly below its 20-day and 200-day moving averages against the dollar despite holding above its 50-day moving average. Broader institutional attention remains focused on geopolitical spillovers and BRICS payment developments, while the ECB explicitly leaves the door open for additional rate hikes at upcoming policy meetings.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar has softened across recent sessions, surrendering earlier advances toward 0.7240 against the greenback following a surge in U.S. producer prices and rising Treasury yields. Positioning remains stretched, with leveraged funds holding an extended net long of 50,250 contracts, while the currency trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages against the dollar. Soaring commodity prices have offered mixed protection, as broader G10 flows turn defensive ahead of today's U.S. inflation data.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar softened 0.20% on its G10 composite day, tracking beneath its 20-day and 50-day moving averages against the greenback ahead of the forthcoming domestic August CPI release. Bilateral trade tensions escalated after President Donald Trump labeled the bilateral exchange rate gap "unacceptable," noting that returning to parity would demand an approximate 38% appreciation of the loonie. Despite trade frictions, the currency has exhibited resilience against U.S. dollar strength, insulated by elevated global energy benchmarks as crude oil trades above $100 per barrel. Markets are looking past the Bank of Canada's recent rate decision to evaluate whether domestic underlying inflation will warrant extended policy divergence from the Federal Reserve.

CHF.catalyst: The Swiss franc trades under modest pressure, down 0.16% on the day and 0.53% over the week on its G10 composite, with USD/CHF holding above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. Disinflationary domestic trends and resilient Swiss labor data have kept the Swiss National Bank cautious, with Chairman Martin Schlegel reiterating that negative interest rates remain possible if excessive franc appreciation threatens price stability. The SNB has emphasized that its willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market has increased to shield domestic exporters. With the SNB widely anticipated to maintain its policy rate anchored at 0%, widening yield differentials against the United States continue to cap the franc's upward momentum.
